question: Should the existing bundled 1Password plugin be expanded to resolve configuration SecretRefs through a host-provided `op` executable under the proposed authentication and executable-trust model?
rationale: This is an opt-in but security-sensitive product boundary: it determines whether OpenClaw should ship a credential-bearing local-executable resolver and which operational deployment contract is acceptable.

options.title: Approve the bundled resolver model
options.body: Accept the opt-in plugin-managed resolver, authorize its dependency change, and require the current executable and environment protections to remain covered by focused tests and deployment documentation.

options.title: Keep the broker-only plugin boundary
options.body: Decline SecretRef resolution in the bundled plugin and direct the capability to an external plugin or explicitly documented manual exec-provider setup.

options.title: Require a narrower trust contract
options.body: Keep the feature pending while owners define stricter supported `op` installation and authentication requirements before accepting the bundled resolver.

recommendation.title: Approve the bundled resolver model
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in plugin-managed resolver, authorize its dependency change, and require the current executable and environment protections to remain covered by focused tests and deployment documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced both the merged Vault precedent and this implementation, so they can provide the clearest design and deployment context for the requested owner decision.
